metadata.methods_description: Participants sat in a sound-isolating booth and heard stimuli through ER-2 insert earphones at about 60 dB SPL. Phase one presented ten one-minute click trials. Phase two presented 33 shuffled trials each of original and chimeric monophonic music, with 0.5 s pauses between trials. EEG was recorded in BrainVision format. Stimuli were controlled with a Python script using expyfun. Participants also completed a musicianship questionnaire.

citation_details.title: An updated herpetofaunal species inventory of Iona National Park in southwestern Angola
citation_details.author: Javier Lobón‐Rovira, Pedro Vaz Pinto, François S. Becker, Krystal A. Tolley, John G. Measey, Bruce Bennet, Bastiaan Boon, Sango dos Anjos Carlos de Sá, Werner Conradie
citation_details.abstract: Angola has experienced an incredible increase of the knowledge of its herpetofauna over the past decade. However, accurate biodiversity inventories remain deficient for certain regions of particular conservation interest. We therefore provide an updated checklist of Iona National Park’s herpetofauna, with 75 recorded species, including five amphibians and 70 reptiles, 40 of these recorded for the first time in Iona National Park. These species comprise ~80% of the reptile diversity of Namibe Province. Therefore, this work recognises Iona National Park as the most reptile-diverse protected area in Angola and is potentially one of the richest in southern Africa. Consequently, this work enhances the importance of specific conservation plans in the area and the need for further investigation into the hidden biodiversity of this region.
